To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the stepwise aggregation equilibrium of DOX is not shifted in the presence of the polymer, and (ii) DOX binds with high affinity to the polymer and the nanoparticles collapse at about 33% binding, which is the reason why DOX-loaded nanoparticles are stable in the absence of excess DOX.

the thermodynamics of DOX loading into nanoparticles can be modelled by considering the coupled equilibria between DOX self-association, binding to the polymer and stacking of DOX onto the polymer-bound DOX.

the loading of doxorubicin into anionic poly(lactide-co-glycolide) nanoparticles is a complex process involving three coupled equilibria and the enthalpic contributions of the three coupled equilibra are: 1) the self-association of doxorubicibn, 2) the binding of doxorubicn to polymer carboxylic acid groups, and 3) the stacking of doxorubic on polymer bound doxorubicin.

at low salt, DOX is loaded into the nanoparticles as a monomer, whereas at high salt it is loaded as a monomer and as a dimer, and at even higher salt it is loaded also as a trimer.
